newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian airline denies interest in TWA takeover.
newsitem.headline: Russian airline denies interest in TWA takeover.

text.p: The private Russian airline Transaero on Thursday denied a report that it was interested in taking control of Trans World Airlines Inc.
"Transaero has no interest in a possible stock purchase of TWA," company spokeswoman Natalia Aleksashina said.
She was responding to a report in Thursday editions of USA Today which said a New Jersey investment group, whose partner includes Transaero, has proposed a deal to take control of TWA.
"Our relationship with TWA can be viewed only from a position of possible cooperation in developing air routes between Russia and the United States, and joint ticketing agreements," Aleksashina said.
The paper said representatives from Strategic Capital Group, led by investor Brian Freeman, presented their plan to TWA at the carrier's board meeting on Tuesday.
The paper said Freeman declined comment, but quoted the vice chairman of the Russian airline as saying he is looking at making TWA a strategic partner and using it as a U.S. feeder.
Transaero has been one of the most successful new airlines in Russia, becoming the country's largest private carrier with 14 Western passenger jets, 13 of which are leased.

The company's total passenger traffic increased 30 percent last year at a time when the industry overall saw a 15 percent drop in passengers, according to figures released on Thursday by Russia's Federal Aviation Service.
Transaero's 1995 operating profit was $27.5 million on sales of $156 million. Figures for 1996 are expected early next month.
AO Transaero was established in 1991. Russia's Aeroflot International Airlines owns five per cent of Transaero.
